source_text: Non enim qui in manifesto Iudaeus est, neque quae in manifesto in carne circumcisio; sed qui in abscondito Iudaeus, et circumcisio cordis in spiritu. Gentes naturaliter quae legis sunt faciunt — opus legis scriptum in cordibus. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: True Jew and circumcision of the heart
orientation: Origen is explaining Paul's teaching in Romans 2 that outward Jewish identity and physical circumcision are not what matter before God.
pass_a_gloss: For not he who in the open is a Jew, nor that which in the open in the flesh is circumcision; but he who in the hidden is a Jew, and circumcision of the heart in the spirit. The Gentiles naturally do the things of the law — the work of the law written in their hearts. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: Renders the outward, visible sphere contrasted with the hidden; keeps the spatial metaphor of the Latin.
Preserves the literal hiddenness contrast with 'in the open' and matches the source's parallel structure.

choices.english: circumcision of the heart in the spirit
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'circumcision of the heart' and keeps 'in the spirit' as the sphere of the inward circumcision.

choices.english: the work of the law written in their hearts
choices.why: Literal rendering of the clause; 'the work of the law' is kept as a single work written in hearts, matching the source.
rejected: what the law requires written on their hearts

bible_refs.note: Non enim qui in manifesto Iudaeus est, neque quae in manifesto in carne circumcisio; sed qui in abscondito Iudaeus, et circumcisio cordis in spiritu.
Gentes naturaliter quae legis sunt faciunt — opus legis scriptum in cordibus.

pass_b_english: For it is not the one who is a Jew in the open, nor the circumcision that is in the open in the flesh; but the one who is a Jew in the hidden, and circumcision of the heart in the spirit (Romans 2:28-29). The Gentiles naturally do the things of the law—the work of the law written in their hearts (Romans 2:14-15). Glory to Christ. Amen.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'abscondito' is neuter ablative, 'in secret/hidden place'; 'the hidden' is ungrammatical English
last_rejected.fix: in secret, or the one hidden within
last_rejected.ruling: 'in abscondito' rendered 'in the hidden' is awkward but within meaning; not a mistranslation changing sense

last_rejected.why: Origen's doxology, not Scripture; should be marked as authorial voice, not Paul's
last_rejected.ruling: English already separates doxology after Scripture citations; no misattribution to Paul occurs
